## What changed and why

The main corrections make the prose match the native signatures and their hypotheses. Numerical non-examples specify their actual Q₂/Q₃ coefficient fields; characteristic two cannot distinguish the signs or means. Three dyadic Gamma arguments were called two; a negative rational argument was confused with its Euclidean numerator remainder; a multiplication test omitted its p=3,m=2 specialization. The transfer/two-lift tests now specify degree one and the dyadic prime. The odd-parity descent test now compares descent([4]) with −descent([1]), while equal source classes have equal descended values.

A Banach-field logarithmic/analytic statement now retains completeness, characteristic zero and the strict radius condition. The algebraic-composition baseline now retains surjectivity of the coefficient map. Nineteen baseline declaration kinds were checked and corrected at their actual pinned declarations. Stale acceptance/hypothesis statements claiming completed proofs, unavailable closure, or a fixed number of source findings were replaced by the actual admitted native outlines and remaining frontiers. Five proof sketches were corrected to match their finite-root and descent consumers. These are planning corrections, not new proofs.

E7 and E14–E27 are independently checked inherited records. The already owned RJW/Coleman findings remain credited to their owners. E18 requires particular care: the least-period Gross–Koblitz logarithmic orbit formula is not itself a raw universal distribution. The repaired weighted/averaged construction is conditional on its exact Coleman logarithm laws and remains admitted/uncompiled; it does not prove a universal raw formula or the later CM applications.

E30: Kubert Proposition 3.3 has too broad an interior regularity hypothesis. The continuous periodic Clausen function Σ sin(2πnx)/n² satisfies the weight-two distribution relation, is C³ on the open interval, vanishes at zero and one half, and is nonzero at one quarter. The alleged scalar Bernoulli classification forces the scalar to zero at one half, contradicting the one-quarter value. The third derivative has an endpoint singularity. Bounded highest derivatives give a sufficient repair, whose minimality is not claimed. No node uses the false classification; the source gap records the limitation.

E31: Robert’s Dwork page uses ζ where the earlier substitution is ξ=ζ−1. The character-linear-independence passage must use functions into the field K, rather than the non-vector-space K×, and its proposition/section cross-references are corrected. These are distinct localized slips in the selected pages.

E32: on S=Q₃ take a₀(x)=x, a₂ₘ₋₁=1+3ᵐ and a₂ₘ=(1+3ᵐ)⁻¹. Both late-factor deviations have norm 3⁻ᵐ uniformly. Paired cancellation gives p₂ₘ₊₁=x and p₂ₘ=x(1+3ᵐ). At x=3⁻ᵐ the even-cutoff error is one. Thus uniform convergence of factors to one does not imply uniform convergence of products on an unbounded function domain. The missing uniformly bounded initial partial product is sufficient. Twenty exact rational controls reproduce the identity. The scalar lemma and norm-one Artin–Hasse application remain valid.

E33: for p=2 and m=1, the primitive even quadratic character χ modulo 5 has χ(2)=−1. The source angular character β=χω⁻¹ has period 20, zeroth moment zero and first moment −40. Every complete-period finite mean at N=20·4ⁿ is therefore −2, so L(0,χ)=2. The correct preceding formula (4) uses β(2)=0. Satz 3’s simplified χ(2) Euler factor gives 4. Six exact rational cutoffs corroborate the all-n period argument. Its simplifying congruence must use the order of ω, requiring even m at p=2, or retain the twisted Euler factor. No node directly cites the incorrect simplification.

Other independently executed exact controls check character means, angular/Taylor means, the normalized complex-root constant, least-period Gamma products, finite Kubert norm/correction-factor models and the averaged Gamma orbit. The p=3, q=2, denominator-13 averaged logarithmic orbit has residue one modulo three; a bound forcing this value into 3Z₃ is false. These finite computations complement the source arguments and are not Lean elaboration or analytic convergence proofs.

| sourceIssueCorrections | `DirichletPadicLFunctions/E18` | The literal product identity is false. Replacing ∏ by ∑ also fails with the printed least-period definition of φ. A repair must account for the differing orbit periods: the candidate additive common-period identity is ∑_h(F/f_h)φ((a+h)/m)=(F/f_a)φ(a), where F is a common multiple of the respective least periods. Alternatively divide each φ by its own period, with codomain/integrality reconsidered when p divides that period. The full corrected distribution theorem is not proved here and must not be imported from the printed statement; withdraw the unweighted distribution conclusion until those obligations are supplied. | The literal product identity is false. Replacing the product by a sum also fails with the printed least-period definition of phi. The corrected additive common-period identity is sum_h(F/f_h)*phi((a+h)/m)=(F/f_a)*phi(a), where F is a common multiple of the respective periods. Alternatively divide each phi by its own positive period in a characteristic-zero coefficient field; p-divisible periods require a separate integrality analysis. The L3 multiplication, root-power, common-period and weighted/averaged logarithm nodes supply an independent lemma-by-lemma derivation under explicit native Gamma and supplied logarithm laws. Their suggested declarations are admitted and uncompiled. The printed unweighted raw-sum distribution and its universality conclusion are not imported. | The final packet supplies the independent common-period derivation after the earlier erratum checkpoint; retain the raw unweighted failure and codomain limits. |
